name: Backend Security & Hardening
description: Backend Security & Hardening standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-BE-SEC applies.

rules.title: Validate and normalize all external input
rules.detail: Apply allowlisted validation for shape, length, range and identifiers before business or persistence use.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Validate and normalize all external input.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Validate and normalize all external input.

rules.title: Use centralized safe exception handling
rules.detail: Return stable safe errors and correlation IDs; never expose stack traces, SQL, file paths, tokens or internal secrets to clients.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Use centralized safe exception handling.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Use centralized safe exception handling.

rules.title: Protect against injection
rules.detail: Use parameterized queries/ORM parameters, safe command APIs and output encoding; never concatenate untrusted input into SQL, shell or templates.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Protect against injection.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Protect against injection.

rules.title: Apply rate limiting and resource limits
rules.detail: Protect authentication and expensive/public endpoints from brute force and resource exhaustion with appropriate quotas and bounds.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Apply rate limiting and resource limits.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Apply rate limiting and resource limits.

rules.title: Run with least-privilege infrastructure identities
rules.detail: Application database/cloud/filesystem credentials receive only permissions required for that service and environment.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Run with least-privilege infrastructure identities.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Run with least-privilege infrastructure identities.

rules.title: Keep security-relevant dependencies and configuration patched
rules.detail: Track supported runtime/framework versions, scan vulnerabilities and apply prioritized security updates.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Keep security-relevant dependencies and configuration patched.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Keep security-relevant dependencies and configuration patched.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-BE-SEC applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Backend Security & Hardening to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Backend Security & Hardening is applied inconsistently across features
common_issues.cause: The project references the standard but does not resolve concrete ownership, thresholds or verification evidence.
common_issues.solution: Resolve dependencies, record project-specific decisions and include applicable rules in implementation/review checks.

common_issues.issue: Implementation satisfies the happy path but misses Backend Security & Hardening failure cases
common_issues.cause: Boundary, retry, security or recovery scenarios were not included in acceptance/test planning.
common_issues.solution: Use the standard rules to add explicit failure/recovery scenarios and verify them before release.
